findings.where: Nav bar (the gummed binding), the home link's logo lockup at top left, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The logo has been recoloured. Its three arches are drawn in pale canary and 'MMM INFRA' is set in canary on the dark binding red. The logo's own colours are grey #404040 arches and a #0070C0 blue wordmark. The client holds no reversed version, so the page has made one up to suit a ground that the logo's real colours cannot sit on.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo the brief says stays and is never redrawn. He would see his mark in colours he never chose. A visitor who knows MMM Infra's blue-and-grey mark from his current site, his documents or LinkedIn would not recognise this one as the same practice.

findings.where: First screen, the handwritten email address beside 'Write to me', and the article specimen's PDF row; the palette's Margin red role ('margin, hand note, document link')
findings.fault: One red marks two different things. In the PDF row it marks a link. In the email address beside the button it colours plain text that does nothing when clicked. The colour that tells a visitor 'this is a link' is also used on text that is not a link.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who has learned from the PDF row that red text is a link, then taps the red address expecting an email to open and gets nothing. Angélique, editing later, would also get no consistent rule for when to use the red.

findings.where: First screen, the white print standing in for Mark's portrait (top right on desktop, below the button on phone)
findings.fault: The print has a soft drop shadow, so it looks as if it floats above the pad or can be picked up and acted on. It is static (parts map p8). It is the only part of the page with a shadow: everything else, including the swatches, the texture sample and the motion-sketch box, lies flat on the paper, with an edge where it needs one.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who reads the raised photo as clickable, for example expecting it to open a bio or a larger image, and gets nothing. The designer of the layout round would also inherit a shadow that has no job and no named level.

findings.where: Article specimen, the title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' (desktop) and the handwritten pull quote (desktop and phone, worst on phone); the motion-sketch box's timeline table against the text around it
findings.fault: Line spacing is not handled alike from one text block to the next. The article title gets two rules (64 px) per line on desktop, so its two lines drift apart and read as two headings. The same title on phone, and the hero headline, are set tight. The handwritten quote likewise gets two rules per line, so on phone its four lines float a whole blank rule apart. Inside the motion-sketch box, the timeline table is set at about 24 px and sits off the rules, while the easing note above it and the totals below it keep the 32 px spacing. The texture note says 32 px is 'the line spacing of every text block', and the page does not hold to it.
findings.who_objects: A reader of the article specimen, who stumbles on a title and a quote that fall apart into separate lines. The layout round, which takes this tile as the type spec, would get three different leading rules for headings, quotes and tables, and no single one to follow.
